source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 132: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Scope and safety (variant 132): treat the hang as an unproven symptom. Record backend, launcher, library/driver versions, world size, placement, scheduler, container privileges, fabric, selected interface, topology, and the exact blocked initialization stage; label every item measured or estimated. Use an authorized disposable allocation only, redact addresses/tokens, set a finite watchdog, and clean up child processes and temporary state on timeout. Do not change production settings until evidence supports a reversible canary.

Baseline measurements: assign a run ID and capture, for every rank, host, global/local rank, expected and observed membership, PID, device mapping, CUDA/GPU/NIC identifiers, software and configuration hashes, redacted rendezvous/store metadata, process-group and collective entry/exit timestamps, last-progress timestamp, stderr/backend debug output, interface/address/route/DNS/MTU/firewall state, peer access, PCIe/NVLink topology, container device/shared-memory visibility, ulimits, and clock synchronization. Verify exactly one process per expected rank, identical world size and rendezvous parameters, reachable peer endpoints, and identical collective ordering.

Falsifiable hypothesis: a rank-specific membership/rendezvous or transport mismatch is causing the initialization stall, rather than a generic GPU fault. It predicts that one or more ranks will have divergent membership, endpoint/interface selection, entry time, or transport error, and that the first failing stage will correlate with that divergence. Falsify it if all ranks have matching membership, rendezvous, interface, ordering, and healthy transport evidence while the failure reproduces, or if an isolated GPU/software fault reproduces with a single rank.

Controlled experiment: freeze versions, placement, environment, seed, tensor shape, timeout, and launch procedure; randomize trial order and repeat enough times to report counts. Run a minimal process-group plus small all-reduce with the same rank map in (1) one node, (2) a reduced multi-node world, and (3) the full world. Use a finite timeout and per-rank barriers; compare the first divergent event, not just aggregate success. In separate authorized trials, pin the verified interface and then restore the baseline; do not combine interface, topology, timeout, and software changes. Record success, checksum/correctness, initialization latency, timeout/hang, rank failure, transport error, and cleanup denominators.

Interpretation and confounders: distinguish rendezvous/membership, collective-order mismatch, DNS/firewall/MTU/routing, wrong interface, NIC or fabric health, GPU visibility/peer access, topology placement, driver/library incompatibility, container limits, resource exhaustion, clock skew, and scheduler or host faults. A timeout or a successful reduced-world run localizes symptoms but does not prove causality.

Rollback and evidence gate: stop any trial that risks shared infrastructure, restore the prior configuration, collect redacted per-rank artifacts, and require correctness plus bounded latency and clean teardown before a canary. A root-cause claim requires the predicted rank-specific evidence, reproducibility across matched trials, and domain-expert review; otherwise report uncertainty and evidence_required rather than asserting a fix.

Falsifiable hypothesis: a rank-specific membership/rendezvous or transport mismatch is causing the initialization stall, rather than a generic GPU fault. It predicts that one or more ranks will have divergent membership, endpoint/interface selection, entry time, or transport error, and that the first failing stage will correlate with that divergence. Falsify it if all ranks have matching membership, rendezvous, interface, ordering, and healthy transport evidence while the failure reproduces, or if an isolated GPU/software fault reproduces with a single rank.

Controlled experiment: freeze versions, placement, environment, seed, tensor shape, timeout, and launch procedure; randomize trial order and repeat enough times to report counts. Run a minimal process-group plus small all-reduce with the same rank map in (1) one node, (2) a reduced multi-node world, and (3) the full world. Use a finite timeout and per-rank barriers; compare the first divergent event, not just aggregate success. In separate authorized trials, pin the verified interface and then restore the baseline; do not combine interface, topology, timeout, and software changes. Record success, checksum/correctness, initialization latency, timeout/hang, rank failure, transport error, and cleanup denominators.

Interpretation and confounders: distinguish rendezvous/membership, collective-order mismatch, DNS/firewall/MTU/routing, wrong interface, NIC or fabric health, GPU visibility/peer access, topology placement, driver/library incompatibility, container limits, resource exhaustion, clock skew, and scheduler or host faults. A timeout or a successful reduced-world run localizes symptoms but does not prove causality.

Rollback and evidence gate: stop any trial that risks shared infrastructure, restore the prior configuration, collect redacted per-rank artifacts, and require correctness plus bounded latency and clean teardown before a canary. A root-cause claim requires the predicted rank-specific evidence, reproducibility across matched trials, and domain-expert review; otherwise report uncertainty and evidence_required rather than asserting a fix.
